prompt: Complete CaseTransformer.upperCase so it copies characters from a Reader to a Writer, uppercasing each one as it goes.
explanation: Reader and Writer are the character-stream counterparts of InputStream and OutputStream: read() hands back one char (as an int, with -1 for end of stream) and write() sends one out. Because the method only depends on these abstract types, the same code works on files, sockets, or -- as in the tests -- an in-memory StringReader and StringWriter. Character.toUpperCase leaves characters without an uppercase form untouched.
hints: Use the classic loop: int c; while ((c = in.read()) != -1) { ... }.
Cast the int to char before calling Character.toUpperCase on it.
Write each transformed character with out.write(...); no return value is needed.
